attempts.summary: Configured node1 (10.100.254.10) as the cluster's internal NTP time source using chrony with `local stratum 10` (self-referenced, since outbound internet NTP is blocked in this environment) and `allow 10.100.254.0/24` to serve the cluster subnet. Configured node2 (10.100.254.11) to sync exclusively against node1 via `server 10.100.254.10 iburst prefer` in chrony.conf, with public ubuntu.pool.ntp.org entries removed on both nodes and systemd-timesyncd disabled in favor of chrony. Verified node2 achieved active sync (`^*`) to node1 at stratum 11 and node1 recorded NTP client requests from node2. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on both nodes: captured boot_id/uptime/service baselines, restarted each node via native `reboot`, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed (proving an actual restart, not just a service bounce), and confirmed chrony auto-restarted and node2 automatically re-synced to node1 post-reboot on both occasions, preserving the internal time hierarchy.
